# MWP Shop: notes for Claude

shop.mw.photography. A static site on GitHub Pages, with Supabase, Make.com and monday.com behind it. Every push to `main` goes live within a few minutes.

## People and approvals
- Matan (owner) approves all copy, design, prices, refunds and terms. Jeinna builds and runs the shop.
- Claude drafts only. Nothing goes to customers and no price or term changes without Matan's explicit OK.
- Don't invent facts, numbers or product details. Check the sales pages or ask.

## Generated files: edit the source, not the output
- `index.html` is generated by `tools/build_home.py` (with `tools/home_try.py` for the "Try it yourself" section). Edit those files, then run `python3 tools/build_home.py`.
- `shop.html`, `product.html`, `account.html`, `support.html`, `legal.html`, `thank-you.html` and `404.html` are generated by `tools/build_pages.py`. Run `python3 tools/build_pages.py .`.
- **Product pages (Oct 2026 redesign):** `presets/` (the Lightroom page: presets and the plugin), `panel/` and `field-guides/` (English `index.html`, Hebrew `he/index.html` and `he.html`) are generated by `tools/build_products.py` from one template, in the home page's look: hero → product bar (name, links, price, Buy; appears after the hero) → RAW/final slider or guide page viewer → what's inside (photo cards) → one feature → what's in the download → FAQs (`tools/pages/faqs.json`) → closing call with two price cards. Styles in `assets/css/product.css`, behaviour in `assets/js/pages/product-page.js`. Edit the content in `build_products.py` (EN and HE side by side), then run `python3 tools/build_products.py`. Every buy button carries `data-add-to-cart="<slug>"`. `tools/unify_pages.py` skips these pages; Matan's original canvas designs are in git history (before the makeover) and `import_designs.py` would bring them back.
- **Hebrew home and shop (Oct 2026):** `he/index.html` and `shop/he/index.html` are generated by `tools/build_he.py` from the English pages, with the Hebrew written into the HTML (from the `HE` dictionary and names in `assets/js/i18n.js`, run through `tools/he_static.mjs` with Node) so search engines can read them. Run it after `build_home.py` and `build_pages.py`. The English pages send visitors who chose Hebrew there, both carry hreflang en/he/x-default, and the language switch moves between the two addresses.
- One header and footer on every page (`site_links`, `menu_button`, `site_footer` in `tools/brand.py`), with a menu button on phones (`assets/js/lib/nav.js`). The shop page is a static catalogue (the four product cards, a comparison table, the bundles: see "The four products" below); `/product/?p=<slug>` forwards the MWP products to their pages and bundles to `/shop/#bundles`.
- Brand colours live in `tools/brand.py` (gold from mw.photography). Use them everywhere, never the designs' original orange.
- Fonts: Google Sans for English, Heebo for Hebrew, on every page (`FONTS` in `tools/brand.py`, added by the build scripts). Don't introduce other typefaces.

## Language
- English and Hebrew everywhere. Matan's rule: on the Hebrew site **everything** is Hebrew, names included. The one exception: **MWP always stays in Latin letters**, everywhere (pages, the beta page, terms, PDFs), never אם־דבליו־פי (Matan, 13 Oct 2026). Product names: הפריסטים / הפאנל / מדריכי השטח של MWP. App and company names are written in Hebrew too (פוטושופ, לייטרום, למון סקוויזי …). What stays in Latin letters: file types (PDF, RAW, LUT, JPEG, XMP, DNG, zip), keyboard shortcuts, the email address, the Instagram handle and hashtags, and the EN switch.
- Hebrew text comes from the `HE` dictionary in `assets/js/i18n.js`, keyed by the exact English text. After that, the names list (`NAMES` in i18n.js, the same as `tools/he_names.py`) turns every name into Hebrew, on every element (including `data-no-i18n` ones). When you add or change English text on a page, add the matching Hebrew entry.
- The Hebrew setting (`mwp_lang`) also sends visitors to Matan's Hebrew sales pages (`presets/he.html` …); `tools/unify_pages.py` adds that and runs `tools/sales_he.py` (names + `EXACT` translations) on those pages.
- The Ambassador terms have a Hebrew version (`TERMS_HE` in `tools/ambassador_terms.py`, needs Matan's review). People who accept in Hebrew get a Hebrew signed copy (`terms_pdf_he.py`, `beta_members.terms_lang`).

## Prices on the home and sales pages
- Every price spot is `<span data-price="slug">` and shows the price set for that product in the admin (`assets/js/lib/prices.js`, reading the `page_prices` view). **The Hebrew pages show the shekel prices, the English ones dollars** (`SHOW_ILS = true` in prices.js, cart.js and bake_prices.py; Matan, 24 Oct 2026). Checkout still charges dollars, so on the Hebrew pages every section with prices ends with a line saying so (`ilsNotes()` in prices.js), each cart row shows "בקופה: $…", and the cart says the dollar total before checkout. Keep those notes until checkout charges shekels. With no price set, the spot stays empty (never $0.00), and a buy button's "· price" part hides (`.pr:has([data-price]:empty)`).
- Product slugs: mwp-presets, mwp-lightroom-plugin, mwp-panel, mwp-field-guides, presets-field-guides, presets-panel, field-guides-panel, full-set.
- Prices show at once: on every deploy `tools/bake_prices.py` writes the current prices into the published pages (and marks them `prices-on`); the browser also keeps the last prices it saw (`mwp_prices` in localStorage). `prices.js` still loads the live prices on every visit and corrects them, so a price changed in the admin shows right away and is baked in at the next deploy. Until prices are in, price spots stay hidden and buy buttons read just "Get …".
- On the sales pages, `PRICE_SLOTS` in `tools/unify_pages.py` lists the price spots in page order. Update it if a redesign adds or moves a price.

## Ambassador Program page (/beta/)
- `beta/index.html` is generated by `tools/build_beta.py` (script: `assets/js/pages/beta.js`). It's shared by link only: not linked from the site, not indexed, and there's no password.
- **Apply first, terms after approval (Matan, 13 Oct 2026).** The page is a single hero with **Apply now**: it opens the questionnaire in a pop-up (about you, photography, editing, values, the program). Sending it (`beta` → `apply`) gives nothing: it saves an `ambassador_applications` row (status `new`), sends it to monday's **Shop Ambassador Applications** board (Make `type: "ambassador_application"`, all answers in the All answers column) and tells Matan.
- **Decisions are made in monday.** The team sets Decision = Approved or Declined. Every 2 minutes while an application from the last 2 hours waits (every 10 minutes for older ones, to spare Make operations: 4 per check, plan 10,000 a month), the scheduler (`applications`, see `supabase/functions/scheduler/applications.ts`) asks Make for the board and acts: Approved → status `approved`, a personal link (`/beta/?accept=<token>`, only its hash is kept, good for 60 days) in the welcome email, Shop result = Waiting for terms; Declined → the decline email; full → Shop result = Program full, no email. Make writes Shop result back and sends the emails from admin@matanwildphotography.com (`application_decided`, Make's Gmail connection 11893994; contact@ was refused by Gmail on 13 Oct 2026, so it was re-signed as admin@). If a send fails, the run waits in the scenario's Incomplete executions: fix the cause, then replay it (it still holds the personal terms link). The email texts (English / Hebrew, signed Emilya) live in `applications.ts`; change them only with Matan's OK.
- **The link shows Matan's terms** (`TERMS` in `tools/build_beta.py`, pop-up with Close and Accept). Accepting (`beta` → `accept`) makes them an ambassador: `grantAmbassador()` (`_shared/ambassador.ts`: the tools, `beta_members` with the terms version and language, signed-terms PDF, Shop Ambassadors), status `accepted`, Shop result = Access given. **Then the account comes first (Jeinna, 30 Oct 2026):** the page says "You're in. Now create your account." with **Create your account** (`/account/?mode=signup&from=ambassador&email=…&name=…`: name and email filled in, a welcome note saying to use the email they applied with) and "I already have an account: sign in". The tools are only reachable signed in with a confirmed email (`get-download` and `guide-view` check the account), never from the beta page itself.
- The old instant `join` is gone: there's no way to get the tools from this page without an approval. The approved person creates their account on My downloads with the same email.
- Change the terms only with Matan's OK, and bump `TERMS_VERSION` in both `tools/ambassador_terms.py` and `supabase/functions/beta/index.ts` when they change.
- Each approved ambassador gets a signed-terms PDF (`tools/personalize/terms_pdf.py`, made by the Personal copies worker): stored privately in the `documents` bucket and attached to the person's Shop Ambassadors row (Signed terms column) through Make (`ambassador_terms_pdf`). The form also asks for Instagram and Facebook.
- Approval gives that email MWP Presets, the Lightroom Classic plugin, MWP Panel and the Field Guides (the guides read online only: `entitlements.view_only`), records them in `beta_members` (with the terms version and language they accepted when applying), and sends them to monday.com's Shop Ambassadors board (`type: "ambassador"`). Applications are limited to 5 an hour per IP; a second application from the same email while one waits is answered "We already have your application".
- The program takes 26 people at most (`ambassador_cap()` in the database; a trigger on `beta_members` enforces it, even for simultaneous joins). When it's full, the page shows "The Ambassador Program is full" and joining is refused; existing members can still rejoin. To change the number, replace `ambassador_cap()` in a new migration.
- Signed terms: made after approval; it sits in My downloads ("Your Ambassador Program terms", `beta` → `signed_terms`, signed in).
- Field Guides for ambassadors: `read.html` (script `read.js`, function `guide-view`). The worker renders each guide version's pages once into the private `guide-pages` bucket (`views/<product>/<version>/`; the `presets` bucket only takes zips), at 1240px for the page and 2480px (`-hd.jpg`, `PAGE_WIDTH_HD`) for full screen; the reader shows the pages without a watermark (Jeinna's call). It shows only the guides in the page's language (each guide's `lang` is worked out by the worker from its file name or text). The page: a guide picker, the pages one under another, and **Read full screen** (clicking a page opens it too). **The full-screen reader (Matan, 24 Oct 2026): no top bar, only the page on black**, with a small floating control at the bottom (close, zoom − / % / +, page number) and side arrows that fade while reading; zoom up to 500% (buttons, + / − / 0 keys, pinch, ctrl + wheel, double-click / double-tap), drag to move around; pages turn with arrows, arrow keys, swipe, tapping the sides, or the wheel when the page fits; Esc closes. On phones held upright, wide pages turn the screen sideways where allowed, else a short hint says to. Guide titles come from the PDF's title or its cover text, in its own language. `get-download` refuses view-only copies. Buying the guides (alone or in a bundle) makes them downloadable.
- Signed-in ambassadors land on My downloads when they arrive at the beta page (once per visit; `assets/js/lib/landing.js`). The home page always shows the home page, to everyone (Matan, 20 Oct 2026).
- Ambassadors can use MWP Panel on 2 computers (buyers get 3): `AMBASSADOR_MAX_DEVICES` in the `license` function.
- Ending an ambassadorship: admin → Ambassadors → End (they keep their licence for life, terms section 7) or End (breach) (their free access is removed; anything they bought stays). `end_ambassador()` in the database does it (admins only) and the scheduler tells Make, which updates Shop Ambassadors (status, end date, a note). Ended members still count toward the 26 places.

## Feedback from ambassadors and testers
- My downloads shows **Send us feedback** to anyone whose Field Guides are read-online (ambassadors and testers): type (Bug, Recommendation, Report, Other), product, message. `beta` → `feedback` checks they're an active ambassador or tester, keeps it in `feedback` (20 a day each) and sends it to monday's **Shop Feedback** board (Make `type: "feedback"`, + tells Matan), with their browser/device in Their setup.

## Testers page (/testers/)
- Link-only page for testers (at most 10 active: `tester_cap()`, enforced by a trigger on `testers`). Testers join by themselves with the **tester code**: name + email + code on the page → `tester` `join` → `add_tester_by_code`, then an **emailed sign-in link** (launch audit, 24 Oct 2026: signing in on the page at once let anyone with the shared code open another person's account; never bring that back). The code never changes access tied to an order (a refund stays a refund). 5 tries an hour per IP. No approval step (Matan, 13 Oct 2026). The code is set and shown in admin → Testers (`tester_code`: the code, readable by admins only, plus its SHA-256 that the function checks; saving a new one replaces it). Remove in admin (`remove_tester`).
- Testers get exactly what ambassadors get (Matan, 13 Oct 2026; migration `20261013000034`): MWP Presets, the Lightroom Classic plugin (from 24 Oct 2026) and MWP Panel to download (stamped personal copies, 5-minute links, daily limit; Panel on 2 computers) and the Field Guides to read online only (`view_only`). Once signed in, the testers page sends them to My downloads, like ambassadors. Removing takes back the free access (purchases stay; an active ambassador keeps the program's access).
- Both actions go to monday's Shop Testers board (scheduler job `tester` → Make `type: "tester"`).

## Payments safety (launch audit, 24 Oct 2026)
- Lemon Squeezy **test-mode orders unlock nothing** (`orders.test_mode`), unless the buyer is the admin (to try the whole flow) or the function secret `ALLOW_TEST_ORDERS=true` is set. Reports leave them out.
- Checkout carries the account's id (`checkout[custom][user_id]`, cart.js): the purchase lands in the signed-in account even if another email is typed at checkout. `checkout[custom][source]` carries the visit's utm_source.
- An order for a variant the shop doesn't know is kept and raised in monday (Shop Orders status "Not delivered"), not dropped.
- **Missed-orders check** (scheduler `reconcile`, every hour at :25, migration `20261024000006`): the last 3 days of Lemon Squeezy orders (store `LEMONSQUEEZY_STORE_ID`, default 502637) against the shop's `orders`. A paid order the shop doesn't have, or a refund it didn't apply, goes to Shop Orders once as "Not delivered" (deduplicated through `webhook_events`, provider `reconcile`). Test orders count only for the admin. It needs the `LEMONSQUEEZY_API_KEY` function secret (the deploy sets it from the GitHub secret), so it follows the test or live key automatically.
- **Webhook signing:** "Connect Lemon Squeezy" makes the signing secret itself (`LS_WEBHOOK_SECRET_TEST` / `_LIVE` on the function); never set or type one by hand.
- The cart refreshes names, prices and checkout links from `page_prices` when opened; My downloads takes what the buyer owns out of the cart and waits up to 3 minutes for an order that's just been paid (thank-you.js marks it).

## Accounts
- **Header and account menu (25 Oct 2026):** visible section links, Cart, EN/עב and the ☰ menu. No separate Account icon since 25 Oct 2026 (Jeinna): the account lives in the ☰ menu's Your account group: who is signed in (or Sign in or create an account), My downloads, **Order history** (`/account/#orders`, `my_orders()` in migration `20261025000003`: only the caller's own orders, test orders left out), My details, Help and support, Sign out (filled in by `cart.js` for a signed-in visitor: `data-sm-who`, `data-sm-signin`, `data-sm-signout`).
- Customers and ambassadors have an MWP account: email + password (Supabase Auth), used across the whole shop. My downloads (`account.html`) has Sign in / Create account, Forgot password (emailed reset link, then "Choose a new password"), and "Email me a sign-in link" as a fallback. `?next=/path` returns them there after signing in; `?mode=signup` opens Create account.
- New accounts must confirm their email before signing in (the deploy workflow's "Account safety settings" step enforces this and an 8-character minimum). Without it, someone could open an account on another person's email and see their purchases. Don't turn it off.
- My details (on My downloads, `#details`; "My details" in the account menu when signed in): name, phone and country (no address: Matan, 13 Oct 2026; an address saved earlier is kept as it is), read and saved through `my_profile()` / `save_my_profile()` (migration `20261013000017`), only for the signed-in person's own confirmed email. The email itself isn't editable there (purchases are tied to it); changes go through support.
- Passwords go only from the browser to Supabase Auth. Never send them to our functions, Make or monday.
- Add to cart on the home and sales pages: their buy buttons (links to `#buy` and the buttons in the `.plan` bundle cards) add that product to the cart and open it (`addSlugToCart` in `cart.js`). The product comes from the price card the button sits in, else the nearest price in its section, else the button's words, else the page's product. Names, prices and checkout links come from the public `page_prices` view. If a redesign moves a buy button, check it still adds the right product.
- Checkout needs an account: every checkout link carries `data-checkout`, and `cart.js` shows "Create your account first" in the cart until they're signed in, then sends them to checkout with their account email.
- Approved ambassadors create their account on My downloads with the email they applied with (the welcome email says so); if it already has an account, the tools simply appear in it.

## Bundles section (31 Oct 2026)
- The four bundle cards on the home page and the shop come from one place: `tools/bundle_cards.py` (styles `assets/css/bundles.css`, small images in `assets/pages/img/bundles/`). The full set leads as a wide card, the three pairs follow. Each card opens with every product in the bundle on its device, drawn from the real thing: the Lightroom Classic plugin's window on a laptop, MWP Photoshop Plugin Panel's Edit tab docked in Photoshop (the fox), MWP Presets on a phone (Lightroom mobile, the collections' names), a real Field Guides spread on a tablet (English or Hebrew by the page's language). Keep the drawn windows in step with the products, as `lrc_preview.py` / `ps_preview.py`. Then: count, name, one line, what's inside (each product with one fact), price with the struck sum of parts and the saving, and the button (`data-add-to-cart`). Cards keep the class `plan` (cart.js and prices.js look for it). Device screens stay in English (`ui-en`). Design and the new copy ("4 tools", the one-fact lines, their Hebrew) approved 31 Oct 2026.

## Customer reviews (Oct 2026)
- Screenshots of real reviews live in `assets/reviews/` with `reviews.json` (one entry each: image, width, height, products `presets` / `plugin` / `panel` / `guides`, alt, source, source_he, lang, featured). How to add: `assets/reviews/README.md` (drop the files in, run `python3 tools/reviews.py`, fill in the entries). No rebuild: the pages read the JSON (`assets/js/lib/reviews.js`).

Hidden while it has nothing to show. ## Personal copies (Presets and Field Guides)
- Each buyer and beta member downloads their own marked copy: their name, email and licence ID on every PDF page, and in a comment inside every .xmp and .cube file (`tools/personalize/personalize.py`).
- The "Personal copies" workflow (`.github/workflows/personalize.yml`, `tools/personalize/worker.py`) makes missing or outdated copies into `presets/personal/<entitlement>/` and records them in `personal_files`. Until a copy exists, `get-download` answers 202 "preparing" and My downloads waits for it.
- It runs instantly when the `PERSONALIZE_TOKEN` secret is set (a GitHub token that can trigger this repo's workflows), otherwise hourly. Uploading a new version of a product file makes everyone's copy again.
- MWP Panel isn't stamped; its licence sign-in protects it.

## The four products: three purchases, presets and plugin together (Jeinna, 23 Oct 2026)
- **The plugin includes the presets; the presets are also sold alone (Jeinna, 25 Oct 2026, with Matan's OK; reverses 23 Oct):** the **Lightroom Classic plugin** (`mwp-lightroom-plugin`, $69.99 / ₪209) comes with **MWP Presets** included: buying it unlocks `mwp-presets` (`BUNDLES` in checkout-webhook). **MWP Presets** alone (`mwp-presets`, $19.99 / ₪59) is just the presets. Migration `20261025000002`. The bundles still give both, keep their slugs and prices, and are named **Lightroom Plugin + Photoshop Plugin Panel** (`presets-panel`) and **Lightroom Plugin + Field Guides** (`presets-field-guides`). The cart (`INCLUDES` in cart.js, the same as BUNDLES) never sells something twice: an item already included by something in the cart isn't added, adding something bigger takes out what it includes, and a signed-in buyer isn't sold what they already own. Lemon Squeezy (one item per checkout, no cart; prices only change in its dashboard) needs a product "MWP Lightroom Classic Plugin" at $69.99 and "MWP Presets" at $19.99. Earlier buyers of MWP Presets keep the plugin they got with it. **Customers always buy the plugin; ambassadors and testers get it free** (Matan, 24 Oct 2026): `add_tester_by_code`, `add_tester`, `AMBASSADOR_PRODUCTS` in `_shared/ambassador.ts`. Tests: a stand-in database run of the real webhook (plugin → plugin + presets, presets → presets only, bundles, refunds, forged and test orders).
- **Minimal pages (Jeinna, 23 Oct 2026):** one idea per section, one big visual, a short headline and at most one line under it; details live in What's in the download and the FAQs. No numbered section heads, pills or info boxes inside sections. FAQs have no label above the heading.
- **The Lightroom page** `/presets/` (both Lightroom tools on one page; since 25 Oct 2026 **two offers side by side** (`#offers`, `.lr-offer`): the plugin with "Presets included" (highlighted) and the presets only, each with what's included, its price and its own Add to cart; the sticky bar's Buy scrolls to the offers; `tools/presets_layout.py`, `own_page=True`, content `m` in the presets dicts plus the plugin's tabs in `P["lightroom-classic"]`, which has no page of its own: `/lightroom-classic/` forwards to `/presets/#plugin`, canonical + noindex, not in the sitemap). Redesigned to say each thing once: **top** (h1 + the two tools side by side: mockup, type, name, one line, where it works, Learn more; then the two offers) → **#presets** (its head: name, line → the before / after slider → 50 · 12 · 33 → the five collections) → **#plugin** (its head → the real interactive window → sort · edit · share) → reviews (both) → FAQs (11, one of them lists what's in each download). No template hero, download list or closing price cards; the sticky bar links Presets · Plugin · FAQs, with the price and Buy (`mwp-presets`). Styles `.lr-*` in product.css.
- **Top bar and ☰ menu (Jeinna, 25 Oct 2026; Matan wants the ☰):** logo · five main links on wide screens (`PRIMARY_LINKS`: Lightroom · Photoshop Plugin · Photography Guides · Compare · Bundles; hidden below 1100px) · Cart · EN/עב · ☰ (no Account icon: the account is in the ☰). The ☰ (`menu_button()` / `MENU_GROUPS` / `SOCIAL` in `tools/brand.py`, behaviour in `assets/js/lib/nav.js`) opens a side panel on every screen size: Shop (all products, Compare, Bundles), More (About Matan), Your account (signed in as / Sign in, My downloads, Order history, My details, Help and support, Sign out), Follow (Instagram @mw_phototours, Facebook MW Photo Tours, WhatsApp +972 53-743-2878). nav.js moves the panel to the end of <body> (the header's blur would trap it), keeps focus inside while open, and closes it with Esc, ✕ or the backdrop.
- **Shop** (`build_pages.py`, `PRODUCTS` / `COMPARE`; styles `.sp-*` in styles.css): no product cards (Jeinna, 23 Oct 2026): a short hero, the comparison table (four columns; the presets' and the plugin's share one price, Add to cart and Details cell, `buy=2` / `buy=0` in `PRODUCTS`, and a `None` answer in `COMPARE` joins a cell to the one before; scrolls sideways on phones, first column sticky), the trust line, reviews, the bundles; schema.org ItemList. Drawn app windows elsewhere carry `ui-en`: build_he.py and i18n.js leave them in English, like the apps. A name whose Hebrew runs the other way gets an `only-en` / `only-he` pair.
- **MWP Photoshop Plugin Panel and the order (Matan, 24 Oct 2026):** the Photoshop product (slug `mwp-panel`, unchanged) is called **MWP Photoshop Plugin Panel** everywhere on the site, in emails, the admin, the database and Lemon Squeezy (Hebrew: פאנל התוסף לפוטושופ של MWP; menu: Photoshop Plugin Panel / פאנל התוסף לפוטושופ). "MWP Panel" stays only where it's the Lightroom Classic plugin's own window name (its FAQ, the drawn window). The bundles too: **Presets + Photoshop Plugin Panel** and **Field Guides + Photoshop Plugin Panel** (Hebrew פריסטים + פאנל התוסף לפוטושופ / מדריכי שטח + פאנל התוסף לפוטושופ; Matan, 24 Oct 2026). The products **always** come in this order: the Lightroom Classic plugin, MWP Photoshop Plugin Panel, MWP Presets, MWP Field Guides (shop table, My downloads `PRODUCT_ORDER` in account.js, `sort_order` 10–40 with bundles 50–80, the Lightroom page's two tools, bundle contents lists, footer, review chips, terms). The home page's Shoot → Edit → Finish story keeps its own order (it follows the workflow). Migration `20261024000009`.
- **Names, the same everywhere** (menu, headings, cards, mockups, FAQs, bundles, My downloads, admin): **MWP Presets** = **Lightroom Presets** (.xmp / .dng) + **LUTs** (.cube; never "Adobe presets"). The **Lightroom Classic plugin** is a separate product (Lightroom's own term, Plug-in Manager; never "panel", so it can't be confused with MWP Panel; its window says "MWP Panel", which the FAQ explains). **MWP Panel** = the **Photoshop panel** (visible labels say panel; page title and meta keep "Photoshop plugin" for search). Migration `20261023000001` renames the download button.

- **The Lightroom Classic plugin** (`MWP-Panel.lrplugin`: its window says "MWP Panel"; Lightroom Classic 13+, early access) is its own product since 23 Oct 2026, sold only with MWP Presets: `mwp-lightroom-plugin` (category `plugin`, no personal copy, no licence sign-in), its zip is the product's file (upload a new version in admin → product). Before that it was an extra download of MWP Presets (`product_extra_files`, key `lightroom-classic`; migration `20261023000002` moved the file, its tutorials and everyone's access). Extra downloads still work for any product (`my_extra_files()`, `get-download` `{ slug, file }`).

Only owners read them (RLS on entitlements, bundles included; a refund hides them) and My downloads lists them under the product. Use **Unlisted** YouTube videos: Private ones play only for invited accounts. Lightroom Classic plugin tutorials belong on the plugin (`mwp-lightroom-plugin`).

The plugin page's interactive window is `tools/lrc_preview.py`, built from the plugin's Panel.lua / Data.lua with look thumbnails in `assets/pages/img/lrc/`; keep it in step with the plugin.

Each effect shows on the photo as a layer limited to the target's area: real cut-outs of the fox, sky and background in `assets/pages/img/ps/` (made once with an AI subject mask, rembg isnet), passed as `data-areas`; holding a chip shows its area in red. No RAW for this photo: Before / After hides the edits; the canvas says "Simulated on this page"; Prepare, Style and Export only list what they hold until the plugin or screenshots of those tabs are here. The line under the window follows the tab. "No way to ruin it" has a photo.

Besides the admin box, the "Upload an extra download" workflow (`upload-extra.yml`, `tools/upload_extra.py`) pushes a public key to a temporary `upload-drop-<run id>` branch, receives the zip encrypted with it (`file.enc` + `key.enc`), uploads it, adds the row and deletes the branch.

## MWP Panel in Photoshop and Photoshop (Beta)
- Both apps keep separate plugin storage, so `tools/panel-license/license.js` works out the device id from the computer, and the `license` function counts a computer already listed under the same name once, but only from the same network (same IP hash; launch audit, 24 Oct 2026: before, any number of computers with one name counted once). The plugin's manifest needs no `maxVersion` (see `tools/panel-license/README.md`).

## Footer legal row, cookies and accessibility (30 Oct 2026, as on mw-phototours.com)
- Every footer (`site_footer()` in `tools/brand.py`) ends with "All rights reserved © year MW Photo Tours" (year filled in by `nav.js`) and `LEGAL_LINKS`: Terms, Refunds, Privacy policy, Accessibility statement, plus a **Cookie settings** button. **The cookie notice** (`nav.js`, 31 Oct 2026, laid out like mw-phototours.com's in the shop's colours): on the first visit a card next to the accessibility button (bottom right; full width above it on phones) with **Accept all**, **Reject all** and **Customize** (Jeinna). The settings window (also from the footer) has Necessary (always active) and real switches for Analytics and Advertising, with Reject all / Save my choices / Accept all, and says the shop uses no analytics or advertising cookies today. The choice is kept per category in `mwp_cookie_consent` ({analytics, ads, date}) and given to the page as `window.MWP_CONSENT` plus a `mwp:consent` event. **Anything added later that sets analytics or ad cookies (Google Analytics, Meta pixel …) must load only when its category is on**: check `MWP_CONSENT` and listen for the event.
- **Accessibility statement** `/accessibility/` (`build_pages.py`, `A11Y_DONE`; English and Hebrew in `only-en` / `only-he` blocks): required in Israel (regulation 35ה, 2013). Adapted from the tour site's statement; it lists only what this site really does, so update `A11Y_DONE` and the date when that changes. Contact: contact@matanwildphotography.com and 053-743-2878, no person named (Jeinna, 31 Oct 2026). Needs Matan's approval.
- **The accessibility menu (31 Oct 2026; our own code, with the features and look of the Nagishna menu on mw-phototours.com, Jeinna):** `assets/js/lib/a11y.js`, loaded by `nav.js` on every page, in its own container outside `<body>` (so page zoom and colour modes don't change the menu). **Button:** the standard accessibility figure, dark on the site's gold gradient with a light ring (the site's colours, Jeinna, 31 Oct 2026; the panel is dark with gold accents too), **in the bottom-right corner of every page, in both languages** (Jeinna, 31 Oct 2026; 54px, 48px on phones; hidden while the ☰ menu or cart is open). It lives outside `<body>`, so page zoom, text size and colour modes never move or hide it. Also "Accessibility" in the ☰ menu (`#a11y`), "Accessibility settings" right after "Skip to content" on the first Tab, and **Alt+Shift+A**; Esc closes. **Panel** (full height on the right, EN/HE with its own language switch, rtl/ltr, focus kept inside): profiles (low vision, screen reader, dyslexia, ADHD, motion sensitivity, easier reading), text size 70–160%, page zoom 100–160%, line / letter / word spacing, readable font, alignment, colour modes (invert, dark, light, black-yellow, high / low contrast, blue-light filter, greyscale, vivid), highlight links / headings / image descriptions, big white / black cursor, reading guide, reading mask, stop animations, keyboard focus, read aloud on click (the device's voices), screen reader support (names the page regions, stops motion), page regions, jump to top / heading / main / menu / bottom, mute media, hide images, reading view (printable), on-screen keyboard (HE/EN), reset, statement, report a problem (email). Settings stay on the device (`mwp_a11y`). It never claims to make the site compliant: compliance is the site's own markup (IS 5568 / WCAG 2.0 AA). The Nagishna slot (`NAGISHNA_SRC`) stays empty: two menus would clash.

## November Sale: 15% off everything, 20% off the full set (Jeinna, with Matan's OK, 30 Oct 2026)
- **1 November 00:00 to 30 November 23:59, Israel time.** One source: `assets/js/lib/sale.js` (`SALE`: dates, 15% / `NOVEMBER15`, full set 20% / `NOVEMBER20`). `prices.js` shows the sale price on every page (the original struck through; bundle cards keep their struck sum of parts and a bigger "Save"), `cart.js` uses it in rows and totals and adds `checkout[discount_code]` to every checkout link, so Lemon Squeezy charges the same price. Shekels round to the whole shekel.
- **The codes in Lemon Squeezy:** "Connect Lemon Squeezy" (`tools/connect_lemonsqueezy.py`, `sale_codes()`) makes them from sale.js, each limited to its products and dates, in the key's mode (test codes with the test key, live codes with the live key). Run it again after the store goes live. It never changes an existing code (the API can't); to change one, delete it in Lemon Squeezy and run it again.
- **The offer box** (`launch_block()`, `LAUNCH_START` / `LAUNCH_END` / `LAUNCH_TEXT` in `tools/brand.py`, same dates as sale.js): before the sale "Starts 1 November: …" with a countdown to the start, during it "15% off everything, and 20% off the full set. Until 30 November." with a countdown to the end, then it hides itself. Prices return to normal on their own after the 30th.

The product and sales pages ship the same Cart icon from `tools/build_products.py` / `tools/unify_pages.py`. Don't bring back a separate Account icon (Jeinna, 25 Oct 2026).

## monday.com sync (what goes there automatically)
- One Make scenario ("MWP Shop · Events to monday", id 7886122, webhook = `MAKE_WEBHOOK_URL`) routes every event by `type`. Its blueprint is generated by `docs/make_blueprint.py` (board and column ids in `docs/monday-map.json`); edit the generator, never the scenario by hand only.
- Events: `order` → Shop Orders + Shop Customers · `refund`/`partial_refund` → order status · `support` → Shop Support (+ tells Matan about refund requests) · `subscribe` → Shop Customers (newsletter) · `product` → Shop Products · `approvals_request` → Matan's approvals back to the shop · `weekly_summary` → Shop Reports · `payout` → Shop Payouts · `ambassador` → Shop Ambassadors (+ tells Matan) · `account` (email confirmed) → Shop Customers, source Account / Ambassador program · `downloaded` (first download) → order Delivery = Downloaded · `ambassador_status` (ended in the admin) → Shop Ambassadors status and end date · `ambassador_terms_pdf` (from the worker) → the signed terms attached on Shop Ambassadors · `tester` (approved / removed in the admin, or joined with the code) → Shop Testers · `ambassador_application` → Shop Ambassador Applications (+ tells Matan) · `applications_request` → that board back to the shop (decisions) · `application_decided` → Shop result, and the welcome / decline email · `feedback` → Shop Feedback (+ tells Matan) · `customer_deleted` → their rows deleted on every people board.
- **Supabase ↔ monday mirror** (migration `20261013000036`): deleting a login in Supabase (Authentication → Users) removes that person from the shop too (their applications and customer record with ambassador / tester rows, free access and feedback; someone with orders keeps their customer record; the admin is never touched). Deleting a customer (any way) sends `customer_deleted` → Make deletes their rows on Shop Customers, Shop Ambassadors, Shop Testers, Shop Ambassador Applications and Shop Feedback (to monday's trash). A customer added by hand in Supabase (not through the shop's API) goes to Shop Customers (`account`, source Shop).
- Make can reject formulas the module checker accepts (a `replace()` with a regex switched the scenario off once). Keep mappings to plain `{{1.field}}` references and clean data in the shop's functions instead. After every blueprint upload, check the next run in Make's history.

## Vercel copy (24 Oct 2026)
- Matan connected the repo to Vercel without moving the domain: customers still use shop.mw.photography on GitHub Pages. The Vercel copy (`…vercel.app`) is a side copy only: `vercel.json` marks every page `noindex` and adds security headers; `.vercelignore` keeps server code, tools and notes out of it. Checkout and sign-in don't work there (Supabase answers only the shop's own address). Vercel builds only `main` (Settings → Build and Deployment → Ignored Build Step = "Only build production", 24 Oct 2026): other branches, including the temporary `upload-drop-*` branches, are never built there. Its GitHub app should have access to this repository only.
- If the domain ever moves to Vercel: remove the `X-Robots-Tag` header first, and move the deploy's build steps (bake_prices, stamp_scripts) into a Vercel build, or the pages lose their baked prices and fresh-script stamps.

## Clean addresses
- Every page also lives at a clean address: /account/, /shop/, /product/?p=…, /support/, /legal/, /thank-you/, /read/, /testers/, and /presets/he/ (etc.) for the Hebrew sales pages. `build_pages.py` and `unify_pages.py` write these copies (with `<base href>` so relative links still work); the old .html addresses keep working. Link to the clean addresses in new code. The deploy workflow copies these folders.

## Fresh scripts
- On every deploy, `tools/stamp_scripts.py` stamps each page's scripts with a version (`?v=`) and adds an import map so every imported script (api.js, cart.js, i18n.js …) is versioned too. This stops browsers mixing an old cached script with new code, which blanks pages. It runs on the published copy only; nothing to do by hand.

## Before pushing
- Serve the site locally (`python3 -m http.server`) and check the changed pages in English and Hebrew, on desktop and phone widths.
- Work on a branch and merge to `main` only when it's ready to go live.

## Admin
- One admin only: jlouise@matanwildphotography.com (Matan, 13 Oct 2026; migration `20261013000031`). The admin page signs in with email and password only, no sign-in links. Two-step sign-in (launch audit, 24 Oct 2026): admin → Two-step sign-in sets up an authenticator app (Supabase TOTP); after that the admin asks for the 6-digit code at every sign-in, and `is_admin()` only answers yes for a session that passed it (migration `20261024000003`). An admin without an authenticator isn't locked out. To change who's admin, edit `admin_allowlist` and `admins` in a new migration.

## Secrets
- Secrets live only in GitHub Secrets and Supabase. Never put them in code or in chat.
